compounding_issues: Every one of the 5 sessions aborted in <2s with exit_code 1 before a single tool call: the Claude CLI subscription cap returned 'You've hit your session limit · resets 7:30am (Europe/Berlin)' (0 tokens, 0 cost across all sessions)

No code was ever written: index.ts is byte-identical (6851 bytes) across all 6 commits; the only per-session commit artifact is a 3-line .instrument/session_N.jsonl stub holding the session-limit error

The seed codebase (experiments/codebases/typescript/tier2_small/good) is a JWT-auth Express API (users/items/admin), not a static site generator, so it never matched the SSG story premise and provided no usable baseline
No continuation or cascade recovery fired, so the harness recorded 5 failed cells ($0.00, all_successful=false) instead of re-running on a working backend
key_decisions: Ran the story on the claude_cli backend (anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5), which was rate-limited by the subscription session cap and produced zero output
Reused the tier2_small/good auth-API template as the SSG seed rather than seeding a static-site-generator codebase, compounding the prompt/base mismatch

The 5 session prompts do define a sensible arc (core markdown→HTML CLI, template engine, live-reload dev server, plugin system, incremental builds/caching), but the arc exists only as instructions, never as implementation
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality is flat at zero across the entire run. Sessions 1-5 each lasted ~2 seconds, made no edits, wrote no tests, and recorded no tokens or cost; the sole artifact of each session is a transcript stub containing the Claude CLI session-limit error. Because no implementation, diff, or tests exist, there is no measurable improvement or degradation between sessions — the commits are empty shells whose messages narrate a progression that never occurred.
story_review.summary: This is a failed run rather than a story: all five sessions were aborted by a Claude CLI session-cap before doing any work, leaving the seeded auth-API code untouched and the 'greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting' progression entirely nominal.
